title: XRP: In-Kernel Storage Functions with eBPF
summary: Lets applications ship lookup and aggregation logic as eBPF programs that run inside the NVMe driver's completion path, cutting storage-stack overhead while preserving filesystem semantics.

title: Specification and verification in the field: Applying formal methods to BPF just-in-time compilers in the Linux kernel
summary: The paper applies formal verification to BPF just-in-time compilers inside the Linux kernel. It introduces Jitterbug, the first framework with a precise JIT correctness specification capable of ruling out real-world bugs. Using Jitterbug, the authors designed and verified a new BPF JIT for 32-bit RISC-V, uncovered and fixed 16 bugs in five deployed JITs, and developed new JIT optimizations—all upstreamed to Linux. The work demonstrates that verified components can coexist within large unverified systems given careful specification and proof strategy.

title: λ-IO: A Unified IO Stack for Computational Storage
summary: λ-IO addresses the overhead of data movement between host and computational storage devices by presenting a unified IO stack that manages both compute and storage resources across host and device. The authors design a co-designed interface, runtime, and scheduler to tackle in-storage computing challenges. eBPF is leveraged to safely offload user-defined compute functions to the storage device. Evaluation against Linux IO shows up to 5.12x performance improvement on synthetic and real workloads.

title: Extension Framework for File Systems in User space
summary: ExtFUSE addresses the heavy performance penalty of user-space file systems (FUSE) caused by frequent kernel-user context switching. It introduces a framework that lets applications register thin, specialized eBPF request handlers in the kernel to serve common-case operations, while retaining complex logic in user space. This hybrid approach avoids context switches for hot paths while preserving the flexibility of user-space development. Evaluation shows significant performance improvements with only a few hundred lines of extension code per file system.

title: Electrode: Accelerating Distributed Protocols with eBPF
summary: Electrode addresses the high cost of user-kernel crossings and kernel networking stack traversal in distributed protocols running on Linux. It implements a set of eBPF-based optimizations—such as message broadcasting and quorum acknowledgment collection—that execute in the kernel before the networking stack, achieving equivalent functionality to user-space code with far less overhead. Applied to Multi-Paxos state machine replication, Electrode improves throughput by up to 128.4% and reduces latency by up to 41.7%.

title: BMC: Accelerating Memcached using Safe In-kernel Caching and Pre-stack Processing
summary: BMC introduces an in-kernel cache for Memcached implemented entirely in eBPF using XDP, serving requests before the Linux network stack executes. Requests are handled within NIC interrupt context, allowing throughput to scale with the number of cores serving NIC queues. Because BMC requires no kernel or Memcached modifications, it deploys on commodity hardware. On Facebook-like small-request workloads, BMC improves throughput by up to 18x over vanilla Memcached and 6x over SO_REUSEPORT-optimized Memcached.

title: hXDP: Efficient Software Packet Processing on FPGA NICs
summary: hXDP runs Linux XDP/eBPF programs on FPGA NICs by compressing, parallelizing, and removing redundant eBPF instructions to fit the iterative eBPF execution model onto FPGA hardware. It comprises an optimizing compiler that translates eBPF bytecode to an extended ISA, a soft-processor to execute it on FPGA, and FPGA-based XDP map/helper infrastructure. Clocked at 156.25 MHz and using only ~15% of FPGA resources, hXDP matches the packet processing throughput of a high-end CPU core while delivering 10x lower packet forwarding latency.

title: Network-Centric Distributed Tracing with DeepFlow: Troubleshooting Your Microservices in Zero Code
summary: DeepFlow is a network-centric distributed tracing framework for microservices that requires zero application instrumentation. It uses eBPF to automatically capture network metrics, trace context, and application-layer requests across the full infrastructure stack. By providing implicit context propagation and eliminating network blind spots, DeepFlow correlates data across components with negligible overhead. In production it has identified over 71 critical performance anomalies across more than 26 companies, reducing troubleshooting time from hours to minutes.

title: Fast In-kernel Traffic Sketching in eBPF
summary: This paper studies how to build high-performance network measurement applications in eBPF, using traffic sketches as a case study. It implements NitroSketch, the state-of-the-art user-space sketch, in eBPF and shows that best practices from user-space networking cannot be directly ported due to eBPF's different performance characteristics. Through lessons learned, the authors improve NitroSketch's eBPF performance by 40% over a naive port, enabling accurate, low-memory network measurement directly in the kernel.

title: SPRIGHT: extracting the server from serverless computing! high-performance eBPF-based event-driven, shared-memory processing
summary: SPRIGHT is a lightweight serverless framework that uses eBPF to replace heavyweight serverless components and enable shared-memory processing between functions. It leverages eBPF socket message mechanisms for shared-memory data passing and event-driven processing, eliminating unnecessary protocol processing and serialization overhead. Compared to polling-based DPDK, SPRIGHT achieves equivalent dataplane performance with 10x less CPU usage, and delivers an order-of-magnitude improvement in throughput and latency over Knative while eliminating cold-start penalties.

title: KEN: Kernel Extensions using Natural Language
summary: KEN allows developers to write eBPF kernel extensions by describing them in English, using large language models (LLMs) to synthesize the corresponding eBPF program. To ensure semantic equivalence between the natural language prompt and the generated code, KEN combines LLM-powered program comprehension, symbolic execution, and feedback loops. Evaluated on a new benchmark of natural language eBPF prompts, KEN correctly generates eBPF programs 80% of the time—a 2.67x improvement over a baseline LLM synthesis approach.

title: Programmable System Call Security with eBPF
summary: This paper introduces a programmable system call filtering mechanism that extends Linux Seccomp with eBPF to express stateful and advanced security policies. It creates a new Seccomp eBPF program type with new and modified helper functions for filter state management, kernel/user state access, and synchronization. Unprivileged users can safely install advanced filters through integration with existing kernel privilege mechanisms. Evaluation shows the system reduces the attack surface of early execution phases by up to 55.4% for temporal specialization and successfully mitigates real-world vulnerabilities.

title: Cross Container Attacks: The Bewildered eBPF on Clouds
summary: This paper reveals that eBPF's powerful tracing features, while beneficial on bare-metal Linux hosts, introduce new attack surfaces in shared-kernel container environments on clouds. Using eBPF, attackers can break container isolation to steal sensitive data, launch DoS attacks, and escape containers. The authors demonstrate successful compromise of five online Jupyter services and Google Cloud Shell, and show cross-node attacks on Kubernetes clusters from three major cloud vendors. They propose a new eBPF permission model to confine eBPF usage in shared-kernel environments.

title: Comparing Security in eBPF and WebAssembly
summary: This paper conducts a comparative security analysis of eBPF and WebAssembly (Wasm), two sandboxing technologies with growing adoption. It examines their security goals, community evolution, memory models, and execution models, then assesses memory safety, control flow integrity, API access, and side-channel resistance. The authors find that eBPF historically prioritizes performance over security while Wasm emphasizes security at the cost of runtime overhead, and suggest language-based restrictions and an improved API access model as future directions for eBPF.

title: A flow-based IDS using Machine Learning in eBPF
summary: This paper presents a flow-based network intrusion detection system (IDS) implemented entirely in eBPF using a decision tree classifier. Rather than simple stateless packet filtering, it maintains per-flow context across packets to classify traffic as malicious or benign. The implementation achieves a performance improvement of over 20% compared to the equivalent user-space solution by eliminating kernel-user data transfer overhead. It demonstrates that complex machine learning inference is feasible directly inside the Linux kernel via eBPF.

title: Femto-containers: lightweight virtualization and fault isolation for small software functions on low-power IoT microcontrollers
summary: Femto-Containers is a middleware runtime that enables secure deployment, execution, and isolation of small virtual software functions on low-power IoT microcontrollers over the network. It uses eBPF as the sandboxed execution model and is integrated into RIOT, a popular open-source IoT operating system. The runtime is formally verified for fault isolation, guaranteeing RIOT is shielded from functions running inside a Femto-Container. Experiments on Arm Cortex-M, ESP32, and RISC-V show an attractive trade-off in memory footprint, energy consumption, and security.

title: bpftime: userspace eBPF Runtime for Uprobe, Syscall and Kernel-User Interactions
summary: This paper addresses the performance and security limitations of kernel-resident eBPF, particularly the context-switch overheads associated with uprobes and syscall tracing. It introduces bpftime, a userspace eBPF runtime that supports kernel-compatible eBPF programs using binary rewriting, dynamic runtime injection, shared-memory eBPF maps, and LLVM-based JIT execution. The system provides userspace implementations of uprobes and syscall hooks, integrates with existing eBPF toolchains such as clang and libbpf, and supports cooperation with kernel eBPF components. Evaluation shows approximately 10x lower uprobe latency than kernel uprobes while maintaining compatibility with real-world eBPF applications and improving deployment flexibility without requiring process restarts or kernel privileges.

title: gpu_ext: Extensible OS Policies for GPUs via eBPF
summary: This paper addresses the lack of safe, programmable, and workload-aware resource management policies in GPU systems. It introduces gpu_ext, an eBPF-based runtime that extends GPU drivers and devices with programmable policy hooks for memory management, scheduling, and observability, while enforcing safety through SIMT-aware verification. gpu_ext executes verified eBPF policies across both host drivers and GPU kernels, using cross-layer eBPF maps to coordinate state between CPU and GPU. The system enables adaptive memory placement, prefetching, scheduling, and instrumentation policies without modifying applications, achieving up to 4.8x throughput improvement and up to 2x tail-latency reduction across inference, training, vector search, and multi-tenant workloads.
